text: Know, my brother — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that the letter alif has an airy wafq; to it belongs the planet Mars, and its servant-spirit is al-Aḥmar (the Red One). It is a letter of powerful effect: when you multiply it by its like, it manifests obedience; and it is the limit of the units. Know, too, that this noble letter has power in the operative deployment (taṣrīf) of all the remaining letters, for it is like the father. Understand this. As for its occult properties: if you want it for love, you write it in this form, as we have set it out for you, in a /fol. 9r./ fortunate hour; and if you blend the name of the person for whom you are performing the operation together with the letter of the square, it is more beautiful and stronger in its effects. You say: I adjure you, O Samsamāʾīl, and your servant-spirits and your helpers of the celestial and of the terrestrial order, and all the servant-spirits of the letter alif; I adjure you that you hear and obey and stir up and disquiet — 252 — by the right of that by which I have adjured you, and by the right of the letter alif and the secrets that God, exalted is He, has sent down within it, upon which none looks save the lofty ones who know God; and by the right of abjad and the occult properties it contains: [I adjure you] that you answer with obedience to that to which I have summoned you, and by that with which I have adjured you. And judge by analogy with this whatever operations and acts are suited to it, and you will succeed, if God, exalted is He, wills, and your operation will succeed.

This is the wafq of the letter alif, whose secret and excellence are renowned among the learned. And if you want it for operations of corruption, do as we have mentioned and you will attain your object. God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

text: The second of the mansions is the mansion of al-Buṭayn, and to it belongs the letter (bāʾ). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it, by the leave of God, exalted is He, a spiritual power fit for wrath and for what has been mentioned above. In it medicine is drunk, and in it the great ones, the sons of this world, and the kings of the earth are stirred into motion, because this decan of Aries is the second, and it is the decan of the sun; in it falls the sun's exaltation, at six of its degrees, on the fourth day of April. The sun is benefic, save that it is hot and dry, of the nature of Mars. Because of its benefic quality and its exaltation in this decan, one works in it for acceptance and for gaining access to kings, for whatever you want of them and whatever you seek from them in it — for your needs will be granted. One works in it, too, for acts of love, for acceptance, and for the attraction of hearts; and strive by means of it toward whatever calls for that. It is also suitable for performing the philosophical arts (al-ṣināʿāt al-ḥikmiyya) and the golden elixirs and their regimen (tadbīr). /fol. 9v./

The third of the mansions is the mansion of al-Thurayyā, and to it belongs the letter (jīm). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it, by the command of God, exalted is He, a spiritual power compounded of heat and moisture, and a middling benefic influence, good for travel, for mingling with the nobles and gaining access to them, and to the great ones, the masters of this world, and the people of knowledge; for al-Thurayyā is an assembly of many stars, and therefore assembly with those we have mentioned is good in it. It has a mighty wafq, which is made during its exaltation and is carried, and with it one goes in upon the nobles; whoever carries it attains his object from them, and they love him and obey him in his affair, and none opposes him in what he wants and seeks. By it Abū Jaʿfar al-Barmakī was favoured with al-Rashīd, and obtained from him everything he wanted. This is the form of its layout, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

text: And for the cutting off of tyrants and the arrogant: write the table of the basmala on a piece of lead, and place the name of the person sought, as mentioned, in the table of the signet; suffumigate it with asafoetida (ḥiltīt) and red garlic; then bury the signet in a place close beside a fire that burns perpetually. And beware of letting the fire reach the lead, for then the one against whom that is done perishes and dies, and you are the one answerable for him on the Day of Resurrection. This is its form. And these are the names which you say over the aforementioned signet: O God, I ask You by the right of Your mighty Name, which is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", before which faces are humbled, to which necks bow down, before which voices are hushed, and in dread of which hearts quake — I ask You to bless /fol. 32r./ and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, and to his family and his companions, and to grant peace; and that You fulfil my need concerning So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. O God, if You know that he will turn back from that which he is in, then guide him and grant him success; and if You know that he will not turn back from that which he is in, then send down upon him Your affliction, Your wrath, and Your displeasure, and destroy him — O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), O God, O God — seven times. And you make this invocation seven hundred times; for the one against whom it is done, God destroys him or guides him. So fear God, exalted is He. And God is the granter of success in what is right.

And if you write the noble basmala, as I shall draw it for you, in the middle of a circle, and write within the circle and around it Muḥammad is the Messenger of God; and those who are with him are severe against the unbelievers (Q 48:29) to the end of the sura, and suffumigate it with everything of sweet fragrance at an auspicious time, and carry it — then you become awe-inspiring, magnified, and honoured in the sight of everyone; and none sees you but he loves you and seeks your company and your companionship, so much so that women incline toward you and toward intimacy with you. So fear God, exalted is He, in secret and in the open. And God is the granter of success. And this is the form of the circle, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

text: And this is a love-procuring formula upon the noble Sūrat al-Fātiḥa. You say: /fol. 62r./ In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 1:1–2). Take charge, O Jibrīl, you and your servant-spirits (khuddām) and your helpers, by the right of God — al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Jabbār (the Compeller), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing). I ask you, O Jibrīl, that you cast the love of 202 son of 202 into the heart of 202, by the right of The All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 1:3). O Jawād (Munificent One), O Jamīl (Beautiful One)! Take charge, O Mīkāʾīl, hearing and obeying, and cast the love of 212 into the heart of 202. Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4). And by the right of God — al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Mājid (the Glorious) — take charge, O Isrāfīl, you and your helpers, and cast the love of 202 into the heart of 202. I have made the bearer of this writing of mine victorious and supported over everyone, as God, exalted is He, gave victory to His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — on the day of Badr, and supported him with the names of God; as God supported His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — with the angels: Gabriel on his right, and Mīkāʾīl on his left, and Isrāfīl behind his back, and the names of God, exalted is He, encompassing him about. Shāhat al-wujūh ("may the faces be disfigured")! And faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting; and he who bears wrongdoing has failed (Q 20:111) — by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty". Shāhat al-wujūh, shāhat al-wujūh, shāhat al-wujūh, and faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting! Māhat, bāhat, tāhat, ḥat, maḥat, inṭilāḥā, maḥallā, ahlā! And know, O my brother, that this is a wondrous talisman and a strange secret, which the learned have stored up and concealed out of fear, lest it fall into the hand of an ignorant man and he violate chaste women by means of it. text: When my shaykh, the master Abū ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq al-Sabtī, died, and the washer of the dead stripped him of his garments, I found in his patched cloak (muraqqaʿa) a folded slip, and I took it. And when I had committed the shaykh to the earth, I opened that slip and found in it noble names which I had asked of the shaykh in his lifetime, by word of mouth, and he had refused. Then he said to me: O Aḥmad, take nothing to heart, for you will come to them without weariness and without hardship. And when I looked at them at that hour, I remembered the words of the shaykh, and I invoked God's mercy upon him, and I said within myself: These are the breaths of the men who are truthful with God, exalted is He. And he had been saying, in that state: After my death you will come to them without asking and without weariness. So I contemplated them with a satisfying contemplation, and behold, there was written in it, saying: Let him know into whose hand these names have fallen that he must guard them /fol. 206v./ from those unworthy of them; for they came down with Adam — peace be upon him — and he set himself to look upon them every day and to say: "Glory be to You! How magnificent is Your worth, and how mighty Your sovereignty!" And he mentions of their occult properties a great deal: were I to give you sight of it, you would walk upon the face of the water and your two feet would not be wetted; and if you wished to fly in the air from place to place, you would do so, by the blessing of these noble names. And by them the men of the Unseen conceal themselves from eyes and fly. And when you have recited them and said: "O servant-spirits (khuddām) of these names, carry me to Mecca the Ennobled" — they carry you and bring you back within a single hour; and for that reason there is an excellence in the going and the returning. And they have many occult properties; and were it not for my fear of divulging the secret, and that they might fall to those unworthy of them, I would have displayed of them wonder upon wonder. So be sparing of them, and do not impart them to those unworthy of them. And this is the form of the noble names:

"In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You by the exhalations of the secrets of the light of Your names, and by the light of the shining forth of the splendour of the perfection of Your Throne, and by what You have deposited in the Preserved Tablet that is with You of the mighty secrets of Your names, and by what You inspired to Adam, the father of mankind, and by what You said in Your most luminous speech, which You sent down upon Your purified beloved: And He taught Adam the names, all of them (Q 2:31). I ask You by Your most holy majesty, and by the beauty of the perfection of the splendour of the light of Your generous, mighty, most luminous, most holy Face, and by what You have deposited of Your secrets and Your lights in the heart of the sun and the moon, and by the right of these majestic, generous, mighty names:

title: Faṣl: in which I mention a majestic benefit
note: Two lines of manuscript cipher (p.1697). Cited, not transliterated.
text: And that is that I entered one of the mosques to pray in it, and I found there a brother of mine, one of those with whom I used to gather in the presence of our shaykh, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the master ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq al-Sabtī, and who used to study under him. And when I saw him that day in the mosque, I drew near to him to greet him with peace; and I found him standing erect toward the qibla, looking now toward the heaven and now toward the palms of his hands. So I drew near to him, and I heard him saying: "O God, O Answerer of invocations, O Fulfiller of needs, O Reliever of distresses from above the seven heavens, O Opener of the treasuries of bounties, O Fulfiller of the needs of those who ask — and Your hearing hears the voices — O Forgiver of slips, O Remitter of stumbles, O Merciful to tears, O Sender-down of blessings, O You whose knowledge has encompassed every thing: I ask You, O God, that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad and to the family of our master Muḥammad, and that You fulfil my need, which is such-and-such, by the right of these names: Hā Hā Hī Hī Hū Hū Yāh Yāh Āh Āh. Subbūḥ, Quddūs (All-Glorified, All-Holy), Lord of the angels and the Spirit! I ask You, O Lord, by what is in this slip of the names, and by what is in these invocations of blessings, that You fulfil my need." And he had not completed his supplication before his need was fulfilled. Then he turned and saw me, and he drew near to me and greeted me with peace; then he excused himself to me and said: I was calling upon God, exalted is He, for the fulfilment of a need, and my Lord has fulfilled it for me and bestowed it upon me as a favour. So I said to him: O my brother, I have heard your supplication, but I look and see you gazing /fol. 207v./ into this slip: what is in it? The man said: I will tell you what is in it. It is that I served our shaykh, under whom you and I used to study, for a long while; and he said to me: O you, have you a need? He said to him: Yes. He said to me: What is it? I said: I desire that you teach me a supplication with which I may call upon God, exalted is He, in my pressing affairs, so that it may be answered for me. He said: Hearing and obedience; your right over us has become binding by reason of your service to us for a long time. Then he handed me this supplication and these names; and I have never called upon God, exalted is He, by them but that I was answered upon the spot, in my very hour. Then he handed me that slip, and behold, in it were these noble names; and they are as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided.

text: Let us give an example of this spirit working, so that it may be easier for students of this science. We joined Zeyd and Omer together for love. Zeyd's number is 21, and spelled out in letters it is as follows. Omer's number is 310, and spelled out in letters these are the letters. In this way you write the wafq on thin leather, construct it with these letters, and complete it.
